symptom: A synthetic publisher can verify that its pinned directory FD matches the expected canonical pathname, then have that pathname moved and replaced with a symlink before dirfd-relative RENAME_NOREPLACE. The rename publishes a complete single-link JSON in the moved original directory, while the consumer's canonical pathname no longer reaches the record. A swap before preflight is rejected. This is a deterministic candidate-design counterexample, not an observed production failure.
lesson: A directory FD protects the object used by renameat2, but a separate stat/fstat equality check on a mutable canonical pathname is only a point-in-time assertion. Even when that check passes, a later ancestor rename/symlink substitution can sever consumer-visible reachability before atomic publication. The preflight is useful for rejecting an already visible swap, not for closing the check-to-use window.
guardrail: Do not promote a preflight-only directory identity check as a canonical-path reachability guarantee. Require a separately reviewed namespace/consumer authority model and deterministic post-check swap adversarial fixtures before considering native publication. Keep strict readback and fail closed on lost reachability; do not auto-delete staged or published paths using stale names, weaken no-replace semantics, or connect research to Current BUY/production. Power-loss, mount and cross-filesystem safety remain unproven.
